environment_bug_found_and_fixed.symptom: sapiens2_3d.py exits 0 but internally every frame's torch.compile-triggered CUDA kernel fails: 'nvrtc: error: failed to open libnvrtc-builtins.so.13.0'. Authoritative signal is the printed 'Batch done: N ok, M failed' line, NOT the process exit code.
environment_bug_found_and_fixed.cause: torch 2.11.0+cu130's nvrtc-builtins lib lives at nonstandard .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/nvidia/cu13/lib/ (no RPATH/$ORIGIN entry), while older coexisting cu12 nvidia packages use the expected nvidia/cuda_nvrtc/lib/ path that IS on the loader's search path.
environment_bug_found_and_fixed.fix: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<venv>/lib/python3.12/site-packages/nvidia/cu13/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH before any sapiens2_3d.py/sam3dinov3.py torch.compile-triggering GPU run in this venv.

session_2026_08_26_mesh_shapekey_portabi.goal: user goal: 'como posso abrir a animation do mesh no blender e salvar para qualquer pessoa conseguir abrir?' -- opening was already solved by blender_viz.py; saving so a fresh Blender install with no vaila/script/OBJ folder can still play it was not.
session_2026_08_26_mesh_shapekey_portabi.root_cause: generate_blender_companion_script()'s import_mesh_sequence() swapped mesh vertices per-frame from a Python module dict (_MESH_STATE) via a bpy.app.handlers.frame_change_post callback. Neither a dict nor a registered handler is a Blender data-block, so File > Save As kept the BVH skeleton but froze the mesh at whatever frame was current when saved.
session_2026_08_26_mesh_shapekey_portabi.fix: rewrote import_mesh_sequence() to bake the whole sequence into the mesh's native Shape Keys -- one key per frame (frame_{i:06d}), each keyframed value=1 only on its own frame with CONSTANT interpolation (bpy.context.preferences.edit.keyframe_new_interpolation_type, restored after) so frames swap discretely. Shape keys and their keyframes are real data-blocks, so this saves/reloads exactly like the BVH action already did. Removed _MESH_STATE/_apply_mesh_frame/_vaila_mesh_frame_handler/(un)register_mesh_handler entirely.

blender_5_2_bug_found_and_fixed.symptom: AttributeError: 'Action' object has no attribute 'fcurves', raised after all 631 shape keys and their keyframes were already inserted
blender_5_2_bug_found_and_fixed.cause: Blender 4.4+'s layered-Actions rework moved F-curves off Action.fcurves onto per-layer/per-strip channelbags; first fix attempt walked mesh.shape_keys.animation_data.action.fcurves post-hoc to set CONSTANT interpolation.
blender_5_2_bug_found_and_fixed.fix: set bpy.context.preferences.edit.keyframe_new_interpolation_type = 'CONSTANT' before the keyframing loop instead -- same preference the keyframe-insert UI uses, stable since Blender 2.8, no Action/fcurve traversal needed.
